{
  "thinking": "The round just started and nobody has a plan yet. A fish in side view has an outline that reads on its own, and the tail fin is a clear telltale part. I'll take the pad and sketch it so we can trace it.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish, side view, nose on the left and tail on the right. The outline alone should read as a fish. I'm sketching it on the pad now, so we can trace it. Maya, could you take the tail fin once I've drawn it?",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "point": [26, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[26, 10], [22, 6], [15, 5], [9, 7], [7, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[7, 10], [9, 13], [15, 15], [22, 14], [26, 10]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 26, "y0": 10, "x1": 30, "y1": 6},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 26, "y0": 10, "x1": 30, "y1": 14},
    {"type": "label", "x": 10, "y": 9, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish, side view, nose left, tail right. Start at tail base (26,10). Stroke 1 top line to nose, stroke 2 bottom line back to tail, strokes 3-4 tail fin branches from start. Need to trace 1 first, then 2, then fin. Maya offered the tail fin."
}
